source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 137: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: Scenario variant 137: Make the choice conditional on measurements; do not invent hardware facts. Assume a fixed model/checkpoint and precision, GPU count/type, usable memory in GiB, placement, interconnect, software and clock policy, request-length distribution, concurrency, arrival rate, batching, and explicit p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, TTFT, and TPOT targets in ms. Define throughput units plus quality, error-rate, availability, and memory-headroom gates. Pre-register the hypothesis that, at the named load and fixed gates, the selected feasible configuration reduces held-out p99 latency by at least M ms or M% versus the best feasible alternative, with M fixed before testing; otherwise conclude inconclusive. Enumerate feasible tensor-parallel degrees and pipeline layer partitions. Measure TP per-GPU shard memory, collective bytes/time, topology, synchronization, and stragglers; measure PP stage balance, activation memory/transfers, microbatch count, pipeline bubbles, queueing, and reconfiguration cost. Run randomized repeated paired trials on isolated identical hardware with the same traces, warm-up, seeds, and software; separate tuning from held-out evaluation, stratify by prompt/output length and load, and report confidence intervals. Record latency, throughput, memory, utilization, communication, bubbles, queueing, quality, errors, and recovery in stated units. Accept only configurations passing every gate; perform only authorized, isolated failure/recovery tests, preserve a known-good configuration, and define timeout, rollback, and data-integrity checks. Control thermal state, background load, caching, kernel selection, tokenization, and autoscaling; report residual confounding and evidence required before production.
